title: ARPAPED Ecosystem Resolution Record
description: The written record blueprint/1-CYCLE.md Phase 0 Gate 25 requires -- naming which pillar(s) this ecosystem adopts (README.md 'Three independently adoptable pillars') and, for each adopted pillar, what actually got resolved. Written ONCE when a genuinely NEW ecosystem root is established (never re-decided by a cycle continuing an existing one -- 1-CYCLE.md Phase 0 step 2/Gate 35); a continuing cycle's own checkpoint.ecosystem_resolution_ref just points back at this same file. Mutable, current-composition truth, not a historical log -- contrast verification-record/episode (never overwritten): re-save this if the ecosystem's own pillar composition genuinely changes later (e.g. adding the DEP pillar to a project that started Bridge-only).

resolution_id.description: Stable identifier for this resolution act, referenced by checkpoint.ecosystem_resolution_ref and agent-cycle-report.schema.json's own ecosystem_resolution_ref.

ecosystem_root.description: This application's own authoritative root (2-RULES.md 'ecosystem root' glossary entry) -- scoped per application, never per repo.

project_kind.description: Whether `ecosystem_root` was a brand-new, empty project or an already-existing one this pillar combination is being added to (packs/README.md 'Starting the Bootstrap agent'). Never inferred from what the Builder happens to find on disk, and never left implicit -- the wrong guess here is exactly how a real run went wrong: given an existing project, a Builder invented a whole fake application (Bridge-shaped capability/contract/manifest/executor files, and in the wrong language) instead of recognizing the existing project just needed the adopted pillar(s)' own tooling merged into it, untouched otherwise.

app_runtimes.description: The `app_runtimes` Bootstrap question's own answer -- does this application have a backend, a frontend, or both (packs/README.md 'Starting the Bootstrap agent'). Recorded here regardless of whether the Bridge pillar was adopted: when it was, this is ALSO reflected as one `pillars.bridge.runtimes[]` entry per runtime named here, but a Bridge-free ecosystem has nowhere else this answer would ever be written down, and the Builder still needs to know it.

app_language.description: The application's own implementation language, per runtime -- the `app_language_backend`/`app_language_frontend` Bootstrap questions' own answers (packs/bootstrap.py's own `_QUESTIONS`), recorded verbatim. Present ONLY when at least one of those questions was actually asked and answered, which only happens when the Bridge pillar was NOT adopted for that runtime: with a Bridge, `pillars.bridge.runtimes[].language` already answers this per runtime, so this key is legitimately ABSENT for a Bridge-adopting ecosystem -- expected, not a gap; look there instead. Never both silently absent AND actually relevant: a Bridge-free runtime with a genuinely undecided language still records the literal string "Not yet / I don't know", never omits the key. Real, observed failure this field exists to fix: an ecosystem was resolved with a real app_language answer ("C#") that was asked, given, and then never stored anywhere -- the Builder agent had no way to know it and built the application in the wrong language entirely.

pillars.description: Which pillar(s) this ecosystem adopted, and what each one resolved to. Presence of a key means that pillar is adopted; at least one key is required -- an ecosystem adopting none of the three is not a valid resolution. Offered as explicit options when this ecosystem root was first established, never defaulted silently (1-CYCLE.md Phase 0 Gate 35; packs/README.md names the available combinations).

bridge.description: Present only when the Bridge pillar is adopted. One entry per runtime the goal's consumer surface actually executes in (2-RULES.md Bridge glossary -- never assume a backend Bridge alone covers another entry point's own requests).

name.description: e.g. "backend", "frontend" -- whatever this runtime is called in this ecosystem.

language.description: What this runtime's own Bridge (Registry/Policy/Selector/Assembler/dispatch) is actually implemented in -- e.g. "Python", "Go". Never inferred from a file extension or left implicit (2-RULES.md "No silent defaults on what resolution depends on") -- explicit, because starterkit/'s own Python (backend) / JavaScript (frontend) code is a REFERENCE implementation, not the only option: a different answer here means this runtime's Bridge was ported into that language from the reference, not copied verbatim (packs/README.md "Starting the Bootstrap agent").

bridge.description: Path to this runtime's own resolved canonical Bridge.

registry.description: Path to this runtime's own resolved canonical Registry.

implementation_map.description: Every required primitive (execution boundary, discovery/Registry, policy, capability model, component model, packaging model, implementation model, connector model, resource execution -- 2-RULES.md resolution table) mapped to the authoritative artifact resolved for it. Generic object: keys are whichever primitives this ecosystem actually needed to resolve.

dep.description: Present only when the DEP pillar is adopted.

dep_root.description: Path to this ecosystem's own copy of the DEP pillar's tooling (packs/dep.yaml).

episodes_dir.description: This ecosystem's own episode corpus directory (blueprint.dep.episode_store).

cycles.description: Present only when the Cycles pillar is adopted. Mostly confirmatory -- the Cycles pillar is methodology, not infrastructure, so there is little to "resolve" beyond naming which cycle/rules doc this ecosystem follows.

combine_with_applied.description: Which cross-pillar wiring (each pack's own combine_with: notes, packs/README.md) was actually applied, for an ecosystem adopting more than one pillar. Empty or absent for a single-pillar ecosystem -- there is nothing to combine.

hook.description: e.g. "bridge.event_sink", "dep.finish_cycle_catalog_path" -- names which combine_with: entry this is.

applied.description: Whether this hook was actually wired, not just available.

detail.description: What was actually done, or why it was left unwired.

resolved_at.description: When this ecosystem's pillar composition was resolved (or last changed).

resolved_by.description: Optional agent/operator identity that made this resolution -- e.g. useful when one agent prepares the ecosystem and a second builds on it.
